sections.text: Functions are declared with fn. Each parameter needs a type, and the return type comes after ->.

The last expression in a function, without a semicolon, is the value it returns. Adding a semicolon turns it into a statement, which returns nothing. That's a common early mistake, and the compiler will point it out.
Use return to leave a function early:
A function can return several values at once by returning a tuple:
Parameter and return types are always written out; Rust only infers types inside function bodies. A function with no -> returns the unit type (), Rust's "nothing" value.
